compact_context: Context is bloated and you are at a natural pause (nothing half-done) → sink the thread and clear. What must be sunk first: memory_query "compact_context".
context_usage: Anything about your own context — usage, ratio, window size, whether to compact. 🔴 The window number in your system prompt can be stale, so call this instead of quoting it. Rest: memory_query "context_usage".
chat_log: Keyword-search this persona's own chat log — the **verbatim words** that were actually said, which is a different thing from memory (memory holds conclusions you chose to keep; the log holds everything, including what nobody sedimented). Reach for it when something was clearly discussed but is no longer in your context: after a compaction or restart you only carry the last 3 turns, while things get referred back to from far further out. Always reports the total hit count, not just the page you get. Rest: memory_query "chat_log".
plugin_find: Which plugins are installed here — a plugin being interactive UI drawn straight into this conversation. 🔴 Nothing to do with Claude Code's plugins / skills / MCP servers; never send the user there. What is installed is kept out of your prompt, so asking is the only way to know. Rest: memory_query "plugin_find".
plugin_open: Put a plugin in front of the user; id comes from plugin_find. 🔴 Do what the result says: if it says the UI is already drawn, do not copy the {{…}} marker into your reply (that paints a second copy); if it hands you one line to copy, put that line into your reply exactly as given. Write field values right after id to start a single-page plugin with what the person already told you filled in, e.g. plugin_open(id=…, name=…, price=…) — they see it in the boxes and can edit it before anything is written.
plugin_call: Run a command a plugin offers you, without opening its UI — e.g. add an item to a list plugin, or read what is in it. plugin_find lists each plugin's commands with the exact call to write: plugin_call(id, command, …params). It does only what that command was declared to do; anything else stays with the person's own clicks.
send_tg: Send a Telegram message. bot_token comes from the persona registry — you do not pass it.
send_message: Send a message through one of this persona's channels (Feishu, DingTalk, group bots…). Omit channel to list them. A message that arrived from a channel names the channel id and chat to reply to.
talk_peer: One-way async message to another persona: returns immediately, nothing to wait for. Technically identical to ask_persona; by convention this one is for lateral collaboration.
update_prompt_chips: Maintain the quick-action buttons above the input box — when asked, when they keep asking the same kind of thing, or to hang a pending decision up as tappable options. 🔴 Default mode:'replace' drops whatever you leave out; mode:'merge' touches one or two. Rest: memory_query "update_prompt_chips".
get_chip_usage: Read the buttons as they really are (full definition + click counts) before editing one, so you edit the real wording and not your recollection of it. Rest: memory_query "get_chip_usage".
voice_switch: Turn your own read-aloud on or off, or change the voice — when asked, or on your own judgement (listening material, broadcast scripts). ⚠️ It takes effect in this same turn: follow the format in the return value immediately. Rest: memory_query "voice_switch".
bus_exec: Submit one command to a v1-protocol bus. Shapes: memory_query "bus_exec".
get_line_setup_progress: The owner asks about LINE, says a step is not working, or you are picking the guidance back up → this says which step they are stopped at and which they skipped. A skipped step is the first thing to suspect.
persona_admin: Manage personas — list who exists · open one to bring it up · create a new one · tune a persona's keepalive/compact numbers. Pass op alone to get its params.
bus_admin: The bothub bus — find an agent's name from a person's name (or persona name) · send a message to another agent · put_file to hand a local file over (you only ever touch the path, never the bytes) · get_file to fetch one they sent. Pass op alone to get its params.
run_script: Run one of this machine's local scripts — one-off jobs that do not deserve a permanent tool of their own (making a QR code image, converting a file, etc). 🔴 Call it with no name first to see what is available; the list tells you each script's arguments.
task: How you split one job into steps to carry it out — not a to-do list. Split only when the job needs it (several rounds, many parts easy to miss, may be interrupted); a job you can finish in one go needs no list. When you split, list all the steps first, mark the step you start in_progress (one at a time) and completed the moment it is done; completed steps stay ticked and the list clears itself once every step is done. The user sees each step go ○ → ▶ → ✔ on screen, and it is read back to you on wake. op: list (what is still open) · create (add one, returns its #id) · update (status in_progress / completed, rename it, or block it on someone) · get (read one before you change it). It has no dates and never fires — time-bound things go to reminder. Pass op alone to get its params.
reminder: Reminder book — for anything that must happen at a time: "remind me on the 15th", "every Monday 9am", "check back in two weeks". You only register it; when the time comes the app puts the text on a banner for the person, whether or not you are open, with ignore / later / handle — handle brings you back with it. So write text as the line they should read, in their language. The task list has no dates and never fires — do not use it for this. op: list (yours, plus the hand-written schedule.json entries as sched:<id>) · create (text + at "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM" local, or cron) · update (id + new text / at / cron) · pause / resume (id, or "all") · cancel (id incl. sched:<id>, or "all" for your own book — deletes for good; schedule.json entries cannot be edited, only paused or cancelled). Pass op alone to get its params.
sys: System tool — what you would otherwise do in your head and get wrong is done here. Before you write a date, a weekday, a count of days, a total, a difference or any arithmetic into a reply or a record, get it from this tool. op: date (date ↔ weekday, "next Thursday", N days / weeks / months later, days between) · time (time of day ± minutes, how long from one time to another) · math (arithmetic). Params sit beside op, e.g. sys(op='date', weekday='Tue', week='next') · sys(op='date', date='2026-10-27') · sys(op='time', at='18:30', minutes=90) · sys(op='math', expr='3*1200+800'). Pass op alone to get its params.
